title: MESI cache coherence protocol
summary: MESI is a cache coherence protocol for multi-core systems. Four states: Modified (M): line is dirty and exclusive to this cache. Exclusive (E): line is clean and exclusive. Shared (S): line is clean and may be in other caches. Invalid (I): line is not valid. State transitions on read/write/hit/miss/snoop. Bus snooping: caches monitor (snoop) the bus for writes to shared lines.

structure.meaning: Line is dirty (modified) and exclusive to this cache. Must write back on eviction. No other cache has it.
Line is clean and exclusive to this cache. No other cache has it. Can transition to M on write (no bus transaction needed).
Line is clean and may be in other caches. Read-only. Must invalidate others on write (transition to M).
Line is not valid. Must fetch from memory or another cache on access.
M: stay M. E: stay E. S: stay S.
I -> S (if other caches have it) or I -> E (if no other cache has it).
M -> S (write back first). E -> S. S: stay S.
M -> I (write back). E -> I. S -> I.

notes: MESI is the standard cache coherence protocol for multi-core CPUs.
MOESI adds an Owned (O) state for dirty shared lines (reduces write-backs).
MESIF adds a Forward (F) state for efficient sharing (Intel).
MESI requires bus snooping or a directory-based coherence protocol.
Cache coherence is essential for multi-core correctness.
